source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed; modelled on AA SL 2022 Nov P2 Q02). Triangle ABC with AC = 21 cm, BC = 15 cm, angle ABC = 108 degrees.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Triangle ABC, AC = 21, BC = 15, angle ABC = 108 deg. Find angle BAC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 42.8 or the display with an ellipsis (42.7910...). A value cut short without an ellipsis (42.79) earns A0. The obtuse value 137.2 earns A0 (the triangle already has an obtuse angle at B).
parts.notes: M1 for a correct sine rule equation pairing each side with its opposite angle: sin A / 15 = sin 108 / 21, in either orientation. A1 for 42.8.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept 10.8 or the display with an ellipsis (10.7753...). Units not required. Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded angle, e.g. 10.8 from angle C = 29.2. A value cut short without an ellipsis (10.78) earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for angle ACB = 29.2 deg (may be seen in the sine rule). M1 for a correct sine rule equation for AB: AB / sin C = 21 / sin 108. A1 for 10.8. A cosine rule route (21^2 = AB^2 + 15^2 - 2(15)(AB) cos 108, solved on the GDC) earns full marks; the A1 for angle C is then implied by a correct final answer.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's angle BAC in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the area of triangle ABC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 76.9 or the display with an ellipsis (76.8594...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate, including 76.8 from angle C = 29.2. A value cut short without an ellipsis (76.86) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for (1/2)ab sin C using any two sides and the angle between them: (1/2)(15)(21) sin C, or (1/2)(15)(AB) sin 108, or (1/2)(21)(AB) sin A. A1 for 76.9. If an intermediate was rounded, add the feedback: carry full precision and round only at the end.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's values in (a) or (b).

source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed; modelled on AA SL 2022 May P2 TZ2 Q01). Triangle PQR with angle QPR = 1.3 radians, PQ = 9 cm, PR = 7 cm.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Triangle PQR, PQ = 9, PR = 7, angle QPR = 1.3 rad. Find QR.
parts.tolerance: Accept 9.81 or the display with an ellipsis (9.81300...). Units not required. A value cut short without an ellipsis (9.813) earns A0. A degree-mode value (2.01) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule with the angle 1.3 between sides 9 and 7: QR^2 = 9^2 + 7^2 - 2(9)(7) cos 1.3. A1 for 9.81 (calculator in radian mode).

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the area of triangle PQR.
parts.tolerance: Accept 30.4 or the display with an ellipsis (30.3520...). A value cut short without an ellipsis (30.35) earns A0. A degree-mode value (0.715) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for (1/2)(9)(7) sin 1.3, or any two sides with the angle between them. A1 for 30.4.

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 0.758 or the display with an ellipsis (0.757825...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded QR. The answer must be in radians: 43.4 degrees earns A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis (0.7578) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct sine rule equation (sin Q / 7 = sin 1.3 / QR) or cosine rule equation (cos Q = (9^2 + QR^2 - 7^2) / (2(9)(QR))) for angle PQR. A1 for 0.758.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's QR in (a).

source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed; modelled on AA SL 2023 May P2 TZ2 Q02). Triangular field ABC with AB = 120 m, BC = 85 m, AC = 140 m; path along AC.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Field ABC with AB = 120, BC = 85, AC = 140. Find angle ABC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 84.3 or the display with an ellipsis (84.3031...). A value cut short without an ellipsis (84.30) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule with AC = 140 as the side opposite angle ABC: cos B = (120^2 + 85^2 - 140^2) / (2(120)(85)), or 140^2 = 120^2 + 85^2 - 2(120)(85) cos B. A1 for 84.3.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Find the area of the field.
parts.tolerance: Accept 5070, 5.07 x 10^3, or the display with an ellipsis (5074.81...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded angle. A value cut short without an ellipsis (5075, 5074.8) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for (1/2)ab sin C with any two sides and the angle between them, e.g. (1/2)(120)(85) sin B, or (1/2)(120)(140) sin A with A = 37.2 deg. A1 for 5070.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's angle in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: The farmer walks from B to the path AC by the shortest route. Find its length (perpendicular distance from B to AC).
parts.tolerance: Accept 72.5 or the display with an ellipsis (72.4973...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate, including 72.4 from area = 5070. A value cut short without an ellipsis (72.50) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for any correct method for the perpendicular distance from B to AC: (1/2)(140)h = area, or h = 120 sin A, or h = 85 sin C. A1 for 72.5. A slanted distance (e.g. BC = 85) earns M0. If the area was rounded first, add the feedback: carry full precision and round only at the end.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's area in (b).

source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed). Ambiguous case in radians: AB = 10 cm, BC = 7 cm, angle BAC = 0.6 rad.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Triangle ABC, AB = 10, BC = 7, angle BAC = 0.6 rad. Find the two possible values of angle ACB.
parts.tolerance: Accept 0.938 and 2.20, or the displays with an ellipsis. Answers must be in radians: 53.8 and 126 degrees earn A0A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis (0.9384, 2.203) earns A0 for that value.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct sine rule equation: sin C / 10 = sin 0.6 / 7. A1 for 0.938. A1 for the second value 2.20 (pi minus the first). A degree-mode value (sin C = 0.0150) earns A0A0.

parts.label: b
parts.description: Given angle ACB is obtuse, find angle ABC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 0.338 or the display with an ellipsis. Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded obtuse angle, including 0.342 from angle C = 2.20.
parts.notes: A1 for pi - 0.6 - (their obtuse angle C). A bare correct answer earns the mark (one-step part).
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's obtuse value in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the area of triangle ABC (obtuse case).
parts.tolerance: Accept 11.6 or the display with an ellipsis (11.6202...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediate, including 11.7 from angle C = 2.20 (angle B = 0.342). A value cut short without an ellipsis (11.62) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for (1/2)ab sin C with any two sides and the angle between them: (1/2)(10)(7) sin B, or (1/2)(10)(AC) sin 0.6 with AC = 4.12 from the sine rule. A1 for 11.6. If an angle was rounded first, add the feedback: store the full value and use it.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's angle in (b).

source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed; IB quadrilateral-with-diagonal pattern). Quadrilateral ABCD with AB = 6, AD = 9, BC = 8, angle BAD = 75 deg, angle BCD = 62 deg; diagonal BD.

parts.label: a
parts.description: Quadrilateral ABCD, AB = 6, AD = 9, angle BAD = 75 deg. Find BD.
parts.tolerance: Accept 9.44 or the display with an ellipsis (9.43650...). A value cut short without an ellipsis (9.437) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule: BD^2 = 6^2 + 9^2 - 2(6)(9) cos 75. A1 for 9.44.

parts.label: b
parts.description: BC = 8, angle BCD = 62 deg. Find angle BDC.
parts.tolerance: Accept 48.5 or the display with an ellipsis (48.4639...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded BD, including 48.4 from BD = 9.44. The obtuse value 131.5 earns A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis (48.46) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a correct sine rule equation: sin BDC / 8 = sin 62 / BD. A1 for 48.5.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's BD in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.description: Find the area of quadrilateral ABCD.
parts.tolerance: Accept 61.4 or the display with an ellipsis (61.4439...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded intermediates, including 61.5 from BD = 9.44 and angle BDC = 48.4. A value cut short without an ellipsis (61.44) earns A0.
parts.notes: A1 for angle CBD = 69.5 deg (may be seen in an area expression); a route that does not need angle CBD (e.g. CD = 10.0 by the sine rule, then (1/2)(BD)(CD) sin BDC) earns this A1 for its correct intermediate. First M1 for a correct area expression for triangle BCD with two sides and the angle between them, by any route. Second M1 for adding the areas of triangles ABD and BCD (area ABD = (1/2)(6)(9) sin 75 = 26.08). A1 for 61.4. If an intermediate was rounded, add the feedback: carry full precision.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's BD in (a) and angle BDC in (b).

source: Original (authored October 2026, calculator allowed; IB 'sides x and x + k, given area' pattern). Triangle ABC with AB = x, AC = x + 4, angle BAC = 2.1 rad, area 30 cm^2.

parts.label: a
parts.description: AB = x, AC = x + 4, angle BAC = 2.1 rad, area = 30. Find x.
parts.tolerance: Accept 6.57 or the display with an ellipsis (6.57368...). Accept the equivalent quadratic x^2 + 4x - 69.508... = 0. Giving both roots (6.57 and -10.6) as the final answer earns the final A0. A degree-mode value (38.5) earns A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis (6.574) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 (implied) for an attempt to use the area formula with x, x + 4 and 2.1. A1 for the correct equation (1/2) x (x + 4) sin 2.1 = 30 or equivalent. A1 for x = 6.57 with the negative root rejected.

parts.label: b
parts.tolerance: Accept 15.0 or the display with an ellipsis (15.0065...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded x. A value cut short without an ellipsis (15.01) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for the cosine rule with the angle 2.1 between sides x and x + 4, substituting their x: BC^2 = x^2 + (x + 4)^2 - 2x(x + 4) cos 2.1. A1 for 15.0.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's x in (a).

parts.label: c
parts.tolerance: Accept 0.654 or the display with an ellipsis (0.653815...). Accept any value consistent with the candidate's own correctly-rounded x and BC. The answer must be in radians: 37.5 degrees earns A0. A value cut short without an ellipsis (0.6538) earns A0.
parts.notes: M1 for a sine rule or cosine rule equation with AC = x + 4 as the side opposite angle ABC, e.g. sin B / (x + 4) = sin 2.1 / BC. A1 for 0.654.
parts.follow_through: FT from the candidate's x in (a) and BC in (b).
